research_question: In adults hospitalised with acute heart failure, what is the effect of continuous intravenous infusion of a loop diuretic (furosemide, torsemide or bumetanide) compared with intermittent bolus injection of the same loop diuretic on net weight loss (kilograms) during the in-hospital treatment period?
treatment_label: Continuous intravenous infusion of loop diuretic
control_label: Intermittent bolus injection of the same loop diuretic
outcome_description: Net weight loss in kilograms during the in-hospital treatment period (e.g. at 72 hours, at discharge, or until resolution of congestion/decompensation), extracted as mean, SD and n per arm. Weight loss expressed as a positive number of kilograms lost; sign reversed if the paper reports loss as a negative change. Percentage weight change not used. Pounds converted to kilograms (÷2.205). SE/SEM converted to SD = SE × √n; medians with IQR converted to mean and SD with a standard method (stated when done). If n analysed for weight is not reported, the number randomised per arm is used (stated when done). Where a trial reports multiple periods, the longest period within the hospital stay is used and the period is stated. In factorial or multi-arm trials (e.g. continuous vs bolus crossed with low vs high dose), dose arms are combined within each delivery mode so that all continuous-infusion participants form one group and all bolus participants the other (summing n, pooling means and SDs). Arms are assigned by delivery mode, not column position.
positive_direction: A positive mean difference (in kilograms) means greater net weight loss with continuous intravenous infusion than with intermittent bolus injection, i.e. the result favours continuous infusion.
search_queries: continuous infusion versus bolus furosemide acute heart failure randomized trial
loop diuretic continuous intravenous infusion intermittent bolus decompensated heart failure weight loss
torsemide bumetanide continuous infusion bolus injection hospitalized heart failure controlled trial diuresis
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trial (including crossover and factorial designs) in hospitalised adults with acute or acutely decompensated heart failure
Compares continuous intravenous infusion of a loop diuretic (furosemide, torsemide or bumetanide) with intermittent bolus injection of the same loop diuretic
Reports some quantitative data on body weight change / net weight loss during the treatment period (mean and SD/SE, median and IQR, or data allowing an effect size to be computed)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, narrative review, editorial, opinion piece, commentary, theoretical or modelling paper, case report)

No comparison between a continuous-infusion treatment arm and a bolus control arm (e.g. single-arm, observational without comparator, or comparison of a loop diuretic against another drug, ultrafiltration, or placebo)
No quantitative outcome data usable for an effect size (no means+SDs, SE, median+IQR, t/F values, or other extractable statistics for weight change)

Completely unrelated to the research topic (not loop diuretic administration mode in hospitalised adults with acute heart failure; e.g. paediatric, outpatient chronic heart failure, or non-cardiac populations)
moderators_to_extract: Total daily diuretic dose equivalence or dose strategy (low vs high, fixed vs titrated)
Study design (parallel, crossover, factorial; single vs multicentre)
Baseline renal function / eGFR or presence of cardiorenal syndrome
effect_size_note: Pool as a raw mean difference in kilograms with a random-effects model (DerSimonian-Laird or REML, with Hartung-Knapp adjustment considered given the expected small number of trials). Orientation: continuous infusion minus bolus, so MD > 0 favours continuous infusion. Weight loss entered as positive kilograms lost. Only this single outcome is pooled; urine output, fluid balance, mortality, length of stay, readmission and renal function are not pooled.
